decision: Before every command except `history`, compare the files with the recorded events and record a set/remove event for each value that differs
`history` never catches up on edits and only reports what is already recorded
recorded_at: src/troupe/cli.py (diff.patch:61) comment 'reports what has been recorded; never reconciles'; questions.md:7

decision: If `history` runs before anything has been recorded, it still records the starting values as import events, as it did before, without catching up on edits
Edits that only change formatting or comments compare equal and record nothing; the comparison is done on leaf values, not raw bytes
Make `watch` poll file contents about every 0.1s instead of using a filesystem notification API
Detect changes by comparing the raw bytes of each file rather than mtimes
After a change is detected, wait up to 20 checks 0.05s apart for the file to stop changing before syncing
reason: wait for a file being written to stop changing

decision: Watch the config file and every included file, tracking them through a new `Editor.seen` record of the raw bytes of each file read (None if it can't be read)
Pick up and watch includes added by hand; a missing include is watched so that creating it triggers a catch-up
Watch both troupe.yml and troupe.yaml candidate names
`watch` catches up first, then prints `watching <dir>` to signal readiness
reason: so any edit after that line is noticed

decision: Broken YAML or read errors during a watch are printed to stderr and the watch continues; errors at startup are raised (OS errors wrapped as LoadError)
SIGINT and SIGTERM make watch exit 0 through a stop flag
`watch` exits with code 4 if no config file exists at start, rather than waiting for one to appear
options: wait for a config file to appear
reason: fail early when there is nothing to watch

decision: Serialise all commands with an exclusive fcntl.flock on a new lock file `.troupe/events.lock`; `set` holds it while it catches up, writes and records, so `watch` sees no difference
reason: a set's write-back is already recorded by the time watch sees it and yields no further events

decision: Only save the configuration aggregate when it has pending events (`pending_events` instead of `collect_events`)
Add a `Troupe.reconcile` store method built on ensure_imported and record
Put the lock, reconcile and watch loop in a new module `sync.py`, and split `run` into `run` and `act`
Reuse a single Troupe app instance across watch syncs instead of making a new one each time
options: cache in an apps dict keyed by state_dir

decision: Test with 3 new tests (reconcile-on-command, watch, watch SIGINT) using a subprocess watcher fixture and wait_for polling with a 2s timeout
Run a manual stress test of 15 sets against a running watch to check for duplicate events
reason: check the race between set and watch
